traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria for 010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION are satisfied by the current implementation.
1) Core Functionality: Implemented and tested. - The `valid-req-reference` rule plus its helpers read referenced story files, extract all requirement IDs via a regex, and enforce that: - Every `@req` uses a requirement ID present in the story file set by the last `@story`. - Every requirement ID listed after a `@supports` annotation exists in the referenced story file. - Tests in tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts cover both success and failure cases, including real story files and fixtures.
2) Quality Standards (formats and structures): Behaviorally satisfied. - Requirement IDs are extracted from arbitrary markdown text using a robust `REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+` regex, which: - Works in narrative sections, bullet lists, multi-story fixtures, and any markdown section without needing section-specific logic. - Is explicitly exercised on a standard story file (001.0) and a bullet-list requirements fixture (story_bullet.md). - Although the implementation does not use a formal markdown parser as suggested in the notes, the functional requirement—handling multiple formats and story file structures—is met: IDs are found regardless of whether they appear in headings, bullet lists, or plain text, and tests demonstrate at least the main variants (standard and bullet-list stories, multi-story fixtures).
3) Integration: Implemented. - The rule is registered and exposed through the plugin’s dynamic rule loader and flat config presets (`RULE_NAMES` and TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES in src/index.ts). - It follows the same annotation model (`@story`, `@req`, `@supports`) and path-safety expectations as the existing validation rules; path traversal and absolute-path checks integrate with the rest of the plugin’s approach to safe story references.
4) User Experience: Implemented. - Error messages are concise and specific: - `Requirement '{{reqId}}' not found in '{{storyPath}}'` clearly tells developers what requirement is missing and from which story file. - `Invalid story path '{{storyPath}}'` pinpoints problematic paths. - Tests assert not only that errors are raised, but also that the message data contains the correct reqId and storyPath, ensuring clarity and consistency.
5) Error Handling: Adequate and graceful. - Story file loading is wrapped in a try/catch; any I/O or parsing issues (e.g., unreadable or malformed files) result in an empty requirement Set instead of throwing, so ESLint continues to run. - Invalid paths (traversal or absolute) are explicitly detected and reported via `invalidPath` messages. - This matches the acceptance criterion of graceful handling: linting does not crash on malformed or inaccessible story files, and developers receive meaningful diagnostics for problematic paths and missing requirements.
6) Documentation: Implemented. - The dedicated rule documentation at docs/rules/valid-req-reference.md explains the deep validation behavior, error messages, scoping rules, and gives numerous concrete examples of correct and incorrect usage. - This fulfills the requirement to document requirement validation behavior and supported patterns.
While the story’s implementation notes mention more sophisticated markdown parsing, the acceptance criteria focus on behavior (validation, handling different formats/structures, integration, UX, error handling, and documentation). The existing implementation meets these behavioral expectations, is fully integrated and tested, and therefore the story is assessed as PASSED.
